sections.content:
You know *dejar de* + infinitive from B1 Unit 12 (*Dejé de fumar hace dos años*), and you also met *no dejar de* in the sense of "keep on doing" (*No dejo de cocinar en casa*). This lesson adds two things.

First, *dejar de* is not only for habits: it also says that something happening comes to an end (*Dejó de llover*). Second, *no dejar de* has a second meaning in advice and instructions: "be sure to" or "do not fail to". You use it in negative commands (A2 Unit 24): *No dejes de llamarme*, *No dejen de avisarnos*.

sections.title: dejar de + infinitive
rows: Don Fabio dejó de venir con frecuencia.
It stopped raining and we went out.
No dejó de hablar en toda la tarde.
He kept on talking all afternoon.
No dejes de llamarme cuando llegues.
Be sure to call me when you arrive.

sections.content: Read *no dejar de* by its sentence. In a statement about the past or the present it means "keep on" (*No dejó de llover*). In a command it means "be sure to" (*No dejes de ir*). It never means "not stop" in a command, so *No dejes de llamarme* is a request to call.
